questions.q: What is the capital of Australia?
questions.fact: Canberra was built as a compromise between Sydney and Melbourne. Parliament moved there in 1927.

questions.q: Which country has the most natural lakes?
questions.fact: Canada holds roughly 60% of the world's natural lakes.

questions.q: The Atacama, one of the driest deserts on Earth, is mostly in which country?
questions.fact: Some weather stations in the Atacama have never recorded rain.

questions.q: Counting its overseas territories, how many time zones does France use?
questions.fact: From French Polynesia to New Caledonia, France spans 12 time zones, more than any other country.

questions.q: Which nut is the main ingredient of marzipan?
questions.fact: Marzipan is ground almonds and sugar. Lübeck in Germany and Toledo in Spain both claim it.

questions.q: Which country grows the most coffee?
questions.fact: Brazil grows about a third of the world's coffee.

questions.q: Saffron comes from which part of a plant?
questions.fact: Each crocus flower gives three stigmas, picked by hand. A kilo needs around 150,000 flowers.

questions.q: Which of these is not a type of pasta?
questions.fact: Arancini are fried, stuffed rice balls from Sicily.

questions.q: What is the largest organ of the human body?
questions.fact: An adult's skin weighs around 4 kilograms.

questions.q: How long does sunlight take to reach Earth?
questions.fact: Sunlight travels for about 8 minutes and 20 seconds, so you always see the Sun as it was.
Two hearts pump blood through the gills; the third pumps it round the body.

questions.q: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
questions.fact: Au comes from aurum, the Latin word for gold. Ag, from argentum, is silver.

questions.q: How many keys does a standard piano have?
questions.fact: 52 white keys and 36 black ones, spanning just over seven octaves.

questions.q: Which band released the album Abbey Road?
questions.fact: It is named after the London street where the band recorded, and came out in 1969.

questions.q: Which film won the first Academy Award for Best Picture?
questions.fact: Wings, a silent film about First World War pilots, won at the first ceremony in 1929.

questions.q: In sheet music, what does forte tell you to do?
questions.fact: Forte is Italian for strong. Its opposite, piano, gave the instrument its name.
